key: And the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest go in to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made unclean; and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house.
s: After the owner reports what looks like a plague, the priest acts before inspecting the house; Rashi, on 14:36, reads the order as the Torah sparing only earthen vessels, which no immersion cleanses, since other vessels can be immersed and food eaten while unclean.

evidence.words: וְעַל מָה חָסָה תוֹרָה? אִם עַל כְּלֵי שֶׁטֶף, יַטְבִּילֵם וְיִטְהֲרוּ, וְאִם עַל אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין, יֹאכְלֵם בִּימֵי טֻמְאָתוֹ, הָא לֹא חָסָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל כְּלֵי חֶרֶס, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם טָהֳרָה בַּמִּקְוֶה
evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 14:36, ‘that all that is in the house be not made unclean’:] And for what did the Torah have concern? If for rinsable vessels, he immerses them and they are clean; if for food and drink, he eats them in the days of his uncleanness; so the Torah had concern only for earthen vessels, which have no cleansing in a ritual bath.
